standards.name: MIRAGE Sample Preparation Guidelines
standards.abstract: These guidelines cover reporting of sample preparation for glycomics experiments—samples defined as carbohydrates, polysaccharides, oligosaccharides or glycoconjugates derived from biological or synthetic starting materials. They specify what to record about sample origin (including vendor, tissue/cell type, species, or synthesis), detailed processing steps (isolation, enzymatic and chemical modification, purification) and a clear designation of the final sample type. The document is MIRAGE's Sample Preparation Guidelines v1.0 (18 Feb 2016), published under the MIRAGE initiative (authors listed in the PDF) and published in Glycobiology; its purpose is to standardize and improve recording of experimental protocols and reproducibility of glycomics datasets across studies.

classification.rationale: The source is written as prose guidance and a reporting checklist: sections and descriptive instructions for what information must be reported (e.g. "Describe how...", "Specify all steps..."). It does not present a field-level metadata table with concrete data types, nor a sequential DAG of steps; therefore it should be classified as PRINCIPLE.

principles.principle: Purpose / scope: include all aspects of sample generation, purification and modification and improve recording and reproducibility
principles.evidence: "The sample preparation guidelines are designed to include all aspects of sample generation, purification and modification from biological and/or synthetic material. Fundamentally, the application of MIRAGE sample preparation guidelines will lead to improved recording of experimental protocols and reporting of understandable and reproducible glycomics datasets."

principles.principle: Define the sample and describe its origin
principles.evidence: "Here “sample” is defined as any carbohydrate, polysaccharide, oligosaccharide or glycoconjugate that originates from any given starting material. The starting material may be a compound, mixture or cell product used to produce the oligosaccharide sample of interest. The source and/or methods used to produce the starting sample material can vary considerably but minimum information that describes its origin is outlined."

principles.principle: Report general information about how the starting material was generated or obtained (vendor, lab synthesis, natural source)
principles.evidence: "Describe how original starting sample material was generated or where it was obtained. Descriptions may include but are not limited to material produced in the laboratory (e.g. chemically synthesized), acquired from natural sources (e.g. human tissues) or purchased from a commercial manufacturer. In the case of commercial material, provide vendor and applicable item information. Starting material descriptions are further delineated by biologically or chemically derived material."

principles.principle: For biologically derived material, report organism/tissue/cell details and any modifications
principles.evidence: "Biologically derived material includes recombinantly expressed proteins, cells, etc. as well as whole organisms or tissues. For recombinantly produced material, the cell type (e.g. CHO, HEK, NS0 etc.) and growth/harvest conditions should be specified. Any modifications to cells that influence the characteristics of the starting material (e.g. genetic manipulations) should also be stated. For material isolated from tissues, the tissue type, treatments and/or storage conditions should be reported. The species should also be provided."

principles.principle: For chemically/synthetically derived material, document synthesis steps or point to protocols
principles.evidence: "Describe how material was generated. If samples were synthetically derived, provide information detailing synthesis steps or specify where the equivalent reaction protocol is available."

principles.principle: Describe the type of starting material that contains the oligosaccharide (e.g. glycoprotein, glycolipid)
principles.evidence: "Define the type of starting material used or produced that contains the oligosaccharide to be used/analysed in subsequent experiments. These may include glycoprotein(s), proteoglycan, glycolipid, GPI-anchored, free-oligosaccharides, sugar-nucleotides or synthetically derived material but are not limited to these definitions."

principles.principle: Document sample processing under three subcategories: isolation, modification and purification
principles.evidence: "The sample processing is divided into 1) isolation, 2) modification and 3) purification subcategories. Required information for each is described below."

principles.principle: For isolation: report enzymes and conditions used to remove oligosaccharides or modify starting material, including vendor or expression/purification if in-house, and format (in-solution or immobilized) plus temperature, duration, volume and enzyme concentration
principles.evidence: "Describe any enzymes used to for the purpose of oligosaccharide removal (e.g. PNGase F) or for modification of the starting material (e.g. trypsin protease). Specify where it was obtained (vendor) or for enzymes produced in-house, describe expression and purification procedure. Also state if sample material was treated in-solution or immobilized (SDS-PAGE, PVDF etc.) as well as temperature, duration, volume, enzyme concentration."

principles.principle: For chemical treatments in isolation: specify technique for oligosaccharide release or other chemical modifications and provide reaction conditions (temperature, duration, volume, concentrations)
principles.evidence: "Define the technique for oligosaccharide release (hydrazinolysis, β-elimination etc.) or other chemical modifications. Provide details of reaction conditions (temperature, duration, volume and chemical concentrations)."

principles.principle: For modification: describe treatments applied to isolated material, document type of modification, sources/kits, reaction conditions and workflow
principles.evidence: "Isolated material may be subject to a wide variety of chemical or enzymatic modifications. The type of modification and reaction protocols should be documented. If new protocols are used provide a thorough description."

principles.principle: For enzymatic modifications: document enzyme concentration, supplier, biological source, incubation time and temperature and, for novel glycosidases, origin/species
principles.evidence: "Document enzyme concentration, supplier, biological source, incubation time and temperature. If novel glycosidase was used, provide information indicating the origin (i.e. species) of the enzyme."

principles.principle: For purification: specify all purification steps used after isolation/modification and describe materials and methods for each (e.g. SPE, chromatographic methods, stationary phase, flow rates, fractionation)
principles.evidence: "Specify all steps used to purify starting material after isolation/modification steps. Examples of procedures include solid phase extraction (SPE), liquid-liquid extraction or other chromatographic methods. For each method describe the all experimental materials (e.g. stationary phase) and methods (e.g. flow rates, fractionation etc.)."

principles.principle: Provide a defined sample name/designation using conventional terminology and indicate the final sample type to be analysed
principles.evidence: "Provide a designation for the final sample in accordance with conventional terminology. Resources for glycoconjugate and oligosaccharide nomenclature are available in Essentials of Glycobiology (Varki, A., Cummins, R., et al. 2009) and Essentials of Carbohydrate Chemistry and Biochemistry (Lindhorst, T.K. 2003)."

principles.principle: Report the sample name/type (examples listed)
principles.evidence: "Name or specify the type of sample material to be analysed or used in other experiments. These may include but are not limited to glycoconjugates, glycosaminoglycans, N- or O-glycans, glycopeptides, glycolipids, monosaccharides, poly- and oligosaccharides"}],

standards.name: MIRAGE Mass Spectrometric Analysis Guidelines (glycans and glycoproteins)
standards.abstract: These guidelines cover mass spectrometry experiments for glycomics and glycoproteomics, i.e., identification and analysis of glycans and glycoproteins using MS-based methods. The recording modality is mass spectrometric data (raw files, peak lists, processed files) and associated metadata (instrument, software, search parameters, databases). The document is published/maintained by the MIRAGE initiative (Beilstein-Institut/consortium) and updates earlier MIRAGE MS reporting guidelines; it addresses reproducible reporting of experimental conditions, instrument settings, data processing and identification/search parameters, and includes explicit expected data types/locations intended to facilitate data sharing and re-use.

classification.rationale: The source presents an explicit metadata table/checklist where each named item is accompanied by a Definition and a concrete 'Type of expected' (e.g. 'Standard date ‘‘YYYY-MM-DD’’ format', 'URL, dataset identifier/password or short free text', enums like Yes/No). This is genuine field-level structure rather than prose recommendations; extract as a MetadataTable.

standards.name: MIRAGE Glycan Microarray Guidelines (Version 1.0)
standards.abstract: These guidelines cover reporting of glycan microarray experiments in which a ‘Glycan Binding Sample’ (proteins, cells, viruses, etc.) is applied to an array of defined or undefined glycan probes printed on a solid surface and interrogated by a scanner to produce image and numerical data. The MIRAGE Glycan Microarray Guidelines (MIRAGE Commission; Version 1.0, 22 June 2016) provide minimal information requirements to make glycan-array results interpretable and reproducible, enumerating eight workflow areas (sample, glycan library, printing surface, arrayer/printer, array map, detector & data processing, data presentation, and interpretation). The document was produced by the MIRAGE working group and Commission to standardize reporting, provide templates and exemplar supplementary documents, and to recommend retention of raw/level-1 and level-2 data while requiring level-3 (processed) data in publications.

classification.rationale: Although the main guideline text is prose, the MIRAGE materials explicitly include a Supplementary Glycan Microarray Information Template (a tabular template listing named fields to be filled) and example supplementary documents that present the same named fields. The source therefore provides genuine field-level structure (an explicit table/template of fields), not merely prose recommendations, so the 'table' representation best matches the source.

Sample.AssayProtocol.evidence: The protocol used for microarray binding analysis of Sample should include Sample concentration. Describe the composition of solutions, time and temperature used for blocking (preventing non-specific binding) binding, and washing, as well as application of secondary reagent(s) required for the analyses. If the Sample is precomplexed with secondary detection reagents prior to adding to the array (e.g. anti-His antibody with his-tagged Sample) give the ratio of reactants and pre-complexing time and temperature.

For mono- and oligosaccharides, the structure of each glycan, i.e. the sequence, linkage and anomeric configuration of each

GlycanLibrary.Accession.evidence: When possible, accession numbers assigned by an authoritative informatics resource, such as the GlyTouCan glycan structure registry (https://glytoucan.org/) should be included.

GlycanLibrary.UndefinedGlycans.evidence: Glycans and glycoconjugates can be structurally defined; alternatively they can be purified or partially purified where structures are unknown (“shotgun” glycan arrays), or partially or on their way to being defined (“Designer” or “boutique” glycan arrays).

standards.name: MIRAGE Liquid Chromatography Analysis Guidelines (v1.0, 2018)
standards.abstract: This standard covers metadata for liquid chromatography (LC) experiments used in glycomics and related analyses. It specifies what to report about experimental context (responsible person, timestamps, sample preparation), LC instrumentation and column characteristics, chromatographic run parameters (time, gradient, flow, temperature, injection), pre/post-run processes, detection systems, fraction collection, data annotation and trace outputs, and exoglycosidase treatments. standards.name: MIRAGE NMR Glycan Recognition Guidelines
standards.abstract: These guidelines specify what to report when presenting NMR experiments and data that characterize glycan recognition by receptors (e.g. lectins, antibodies, glycan-binding organisms, or synthetic glycan-binding molecules). standards.name: MIRAGE NMR Glycan Structures Guidelines
standards.abstract: These guidelines specify what to report when characterizing glycan composition, conformation and dynamics using NMR. They apply to NMR experiments on natural and synthetic glycans (including glycoprotein-derived glycans) and include details about the sample, spectrometer and processing, measured NMR parameters, data presentation, and interpretation. The document is published as MIRAGE Guidelines (Version 1.0, 21 September 2020; doi:10.3762/mirage.6) and is intended to standardize reporting of NMR experiments/data for glycan structure determination so that manuscripts and supplementary tables contain comprehensive, reproducible information.

standards.name: MIRAGE Capillary Electrophoresis Guidelines
standards.abstract: These guidelines apply to capillary electrophoresis (CE) experiments used in glycomics/glycoproteomics, where separations (e.g. capillary gel electrophoresis with laser induced fluorescence, xCGE-LIF) produce electropherogram data files (.ab1/.fsa) and processed glycan fingerprints. The document (MIRAGE CE Guidelines v1.0, published in Glycobiology, doi:10.1093/glycob/cwac021) is maintained by the MIRAGE authorship group (Lageveen-Kammeijer, Rapp, Chang, Rudd, Kettner, Zaia et al.) to define minimum reporting metadata for CE experiments: what to report about general features, samples and solutions, equipment and software, capillary specifications, run processes, analysis type and calibration/normalization, and sample injection. The goal is to ensure sufficient detail to reproduce/interpret CE glycoanalysis and to enable data reuse and interoperability with other MIRAGE modules (e.g. Sample Preparation, Mass Spectrometry).

classification.rationale: The source presents a set of named metadata items with explicit recommended formats or enumerated examples (e.g. date format, manufacturer/model, capillary dimensions, CE mode examples). These are concrete fields to be reported rather than only prose instructions, so the material is best represented as a MetadataTable.

standards.name: MIRAGE Lectin Microarray Analysis Guidelines
standards.abstract: These guidelines cover experiments using lectin microarrays to profile glycan-containing samples (e.g., glycans, glycoproteins, cell lysates, cells, glycopeptides) where binding of sample components to immobilized lectins is detected (typically by fluorescence scanning). The MIRAGE Lectin Microarray Guidelines (Version 1.0, April 10, 2023; DOI: 10.3762/mirage.8) were published by members of the MIRAGE consortium (authors include Hiroaki Tateno et al.) to standardize reporting of lectin microarray experiments. The document provides a structured checklist and a template for reporting sample description and preparation, lectin library composition and specificity, immobilization surface and array production, detection instrumentation and image/data processing, data presentation/interpretation, and data location, with the goal of ensuring sufficient metadata to interpret, reproduce and reuse lectin microarray data.

classification.rationale: The source is presented as a structured reporting checklist and an information template with named fields (e.g. 'Description of Sample', 'Sample preparation protocol', 'Instrument settings') and an explicit table/template layout. These are concrete metadata fields intended to be completed in a tabular/template form rather than purely instructional prose, so the 'table' type best matches the source.
